typical_topologies: Serial Wire Debug protocol version 1 is a point-to-point architecture, supporting connection between a single host
point-to-point compatibility with existing host equipment that does not support the multi-drop extensions.

id_routing.description: Interconnect may append bits to AxID to identify the originating master; slave-side ID_WIDTH > master-side ID_WIDTH
id_routing.compliance_note: Returning ID is the WIDER value; routing strips appended bits before returning to the master

fields.ic_name: ARM Serial Wire Debug (SWD) — ADIv5 (ARM IHI 0031C)
fields.topology_type: Two-wire host-to-target serial debug bus (no daisy chain). Host drives SWCLK; SWDIO is bidirectional with explicit Turnaround periods. Multi-drop SWD (ADIv5.2) shares SWDIO/SWCLK across multiple targets in parallel with per-target selection via TARGETSEL.

supported_topologies.name: Single-target SWD
supported_topologies.description: One debug host + one target SoC.

supported_topologies.name: SWJ-DP mode-switched
supported_topologies.description: Single target supports both SWD and JTAG.

supported_topologies.name: Multi-drop SWD (ADIv5.2)
supported_topologies.description: Multiple targets share SWDIO/SWCLK; per-target selection via TARGETSEL.

supported_topologies.name: SWD + SWO trace
supported_topologies.description: Single target with dedicated SWO trace pin.

master_slave_role_summary.description: Arm Cortex-based SoC implementing SW-DP / SWJ-DP + DP + AP layers.
ADIv5.2 — additional SoC with unique TPARTNO+TINSTANCE.

fields.interconnect_role: There is NO daisy chain at the SWD wire layer (unlike JTAG). SWD is point-to-point (or multi-drop in ADIv5.2). On the target side, the DAP fans transactions to up to 256 APs over an internal AP bus.

ordering_guarantees.transaction_order: Strict sequential — each 46-bit transaction completes before the next begins. Posted reads pipeline the data return, but the wire-level ordering of transactions is strict.
ordering_guarantees.posted_read_pipelining: Read N's data appears with the ACK of transaction N+1 (or RDBUFF).
ordering_guarantees.ap_register_atomicity: Each AP register access is atomic from the host's POV.

fields.memory_vs_peripheral_regions: DP registers are accessed via APnDP=0 + A[3:2] — not memory-mapped. AP registers via APnDP=1 + APSEL + APBANKSEL + A[3:2]. MEM-AP CSW+TAR+DRW provides a window into the SoC's memory-mapped system bus.
